body.p: Applicant responds to the Office Action dated February 16, 2024 and requests the Examiner consider the following remarks.

The Examiner rejects claims 1-10, 15, 16, 18, and 21-24 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Patent No. 7,556,462 ('462 Huber) in view of U.S. Patent No. 6,125,984 ('984 Huber). Applicant respectfully disagrees and traverses the rejection.

The Examiner acknowledges that '462 Huber "does not disclose a cargo compartment extending from a forward end, through a forward section, through an entranceway section, and through an aft section to an aft end; and the plurality of trays are continuously covered from the forward end of the cargo compartment, through the forward section, through the entranceway section, and through the aft section to the aft end" (Office Action, pgs. 4-5). For this limitation, the Examiner relies on the '984 Huber reference. Applicant believes the Examiner is misunderstanding the teachings the '984 Huber reference.

First, Huber '984 does not teach "a cargo compartment extending from a forward end, through a forward section, through an entranceway section, and through an aft section to an aft end" and "the plurality of trays are continuously covered from the forward end of the cargo compartment, through the forward section, through the entranceway section, and through the aft section to the aft end" as presently claimed.

More specifically, Huber '984 is directed towards a "ball mat for the loading deck of an aircraft [which] is a known device to support cargo and assist the movement thereof' (Abstract). As Huber '984 is solely directed to this ball mat, Huber '984 fails to disclose or contemplate anything regarding a "cargo compartment" that it goes within. However, Huber '462, the base reference, shows exactly where the ball mat goes within a cargo compartment ([Col. 3, lns. 20- 21]: "Furthermore, in a door region 55, where the ball mats 21 are located..."). Accordingly, ball mats are typically located only at an entranceway of a cargo compartment as shown in Huber '984. It is commonly known in the art that ball mats are located at the entranceway to assist with loading and unloading, and ball mats are not within a remaining area of the cargo compartment. Ball mats have a very specific purpose (i.e., to assist a transition of loading in a lateral direction through an entranceway to loading longitudinally forward and aft in a longitudinal direction). One skilled in the art would in no way be motivated to extend a ball mat throughout a cargo compartment because it would add weight, which is a very important factor for aircrafts, with no benefit (i.e., cargo will not be loaded where there is not an entranceway). If one skilled in the art were to modify Huber '462 with Huber '984, one would replace the ball mat 21 of Huber '462 as shown in FIG. 1 of Huber '462 with the ball mat of Huber '984, which would only be disposed "in a door region 55" (col. 3, in. 21) and not result in "the plurality of trays [being] continuously covered from the forward end of the cargo compartment, through the forward section, through the entranceway section, and through the aft section to the aft end" as claimed.

Furthermore, the trays of Huber '984 are not even "continuously covered" as claimed. In particular, as shown in annotated FIG. 2 below from Huber '984, the flange A of the tray is flush with the mat B (compare with A' and B' of FIG. 5B from the Present Disclosure annotated below), not "continuously covered" by the mat B.

Accordingly, Applicant asserts that Huber '984 and Huber '462 fail to render obvious independent claims 1, 8, and 15 as recited herein. Therefore, Applicant asserts that the rejection should be withdrawn.

In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that all pending claims are allowable and requests allowance of the pending claims.
